title: How Much Does Evertune Cost? (2026 Pricing, Explained)
metaTitle: How Much Does Evertune Cost? $800 Pro, Custom Enterprise
metaDescription: Evertune's pricing page lists Pro at $800/month and a quote-only Enterprise plan. No free trial is mentioned. Here is what drives the bill and who it suits.
shortAnswer: As of 3 October 2026, [Evertune's pricing page](https://www.evertune.ai/pricing) lists one price: Pro at $800 a month for 100,000 tracked prompts across 11 AI models. Enterprise is "Custom", so quote only. Both plans end in a "Request a demo" button, and no free trial is mentioned anywhere we looked. Plan on at least $9,600 a year for Pro, before any ad-management or setup fees an order may add.
intro:
This guide is based on public documentation as of October 2026; we have not tested the product hands-on, and nothing here is a quote from Evertune. Every Evertune price and feature below comes from Evertune's own pages, opened on 3 October 2026. Where a page is silent, we say so instead of guessing.

Our position: Evertune's price is not the surprise. The surprise is how much of what you pay for sits on the "act" side (content and ChatGPT ads) rather than measurement. Buy it only if you will use that side.

sections.heading: How much does Evertune cost?
sections.body:
Evertune publishes one price: Pro at $800 a month. Enterprise is "Custom", which means you get a quote after a call. The [pricing page](https://www.evertune.ai/pricing) shows a dollar sign and no currency code, and every button reads "Request a demo".

| | Pro | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|
| Price | $800 / month | Custom (quote only) |
| Aimed at | Mid-market brands | Enterprise companies |
| Tracking | 100,000 prompts, 11 AI models, daily, weekly or monthly | Everything in Pro |
| Content | 25 AI-optimized articles a month | Unlimited content generation |
| People | 3 onboarding sessions | Dedicated AI Success Manager, customized onboarding |
| Extras | Affiliate advertising partnerships, AI Retargeting | Deep category analysis, AI website optimization, AI bot analytics for your domain, SSO |

The page does not say whether $800 is billed monthly or annually, or what Enterprise costs. As a planning figure, $800 × 12 = $9,600 a year for Pro. That is arithmetic on a list price, not a quote.

sections.heading: Why do some sites still say Evertune costs $3,000 a month?
sections.body:
Because older third-party comparisons reported an entry price near $3,000 a month, and the figure kept getting copied. We could not find it on any Evertune page we opened, and the current [pricing page](https://www.evertune.ai/pricing) shows $800 for Pro instead.

Treat $3,000 as an unverified, probably outdated number. If you are budgeting for Enterprise, the honest answer is that nobody outside a sales call knows yet. Ask for the figure in writing.

sections.heading: Is there an Evertune free trial?
sections.body:
No free trial is mentioned on Evertune's pricing page, plans or FAQ. The only call to action is "Request a demo". The closest thing to trying it is on the [Pro plan sign-up page](https://www.evertune.ai/lp/get-started-pro-plan): after you submit the form, Evertune's team "will be in touch to walk you through your first report" showing what AI says about your brand. It does not say whether that is free.

One wrinkle. Evertune's [Platform Terms](https://www.evertune.ai/legal/platform-terms-and-conditions), last updated 3 September 2026, cover "self-serve" purchases through online order pages, paid by credit card or another approved method. We found no public checkout, so treat that as a sign the model may change, not as an available option today. The [ChatGPT Ads Manager](https://www.evertune.ai/platform/ads-manager) is a beta with a waiting list, not a trial.

![Business person sorting paper receipts into neat stacks at a desk](https://images.pexels.com/photos/7545333/pexels-photo-7545333.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

Without a trial, make the demo do the work. Ask them to run your category and your competitors live, and to explain what the 100,000-prompt allowance counts. If you are screening four vendors, that is four calls before one hands-on look, so cheaper checks come first.

sections.heading: What drives the price?
sections.body:
Four things move the bill: prompt volume, the plan tier, the contract term and any ad-management fees. Evertune's [Platform Terms](https://www.evertune.ai/legal/platform-terms-and-conditions) list the fee types an order page may include. They do not say which apply to Pro, so ask.

- **Prompt volume.** Pro includes 100,000 tracked prompts. The page does not define the unit, and the [FAQ](https://www.evertune.ai/resources/faq) says Evertune samples each prompt 100 times per model. If 100,000 means distinct prompts, $800 ÷ 100,000 = $0.008 per prompt a month. If it means samples, the unit price is very different.
- **Tier.** Moving to Enterprise adds unlimited content generation, a named success manager and bot analytics.
- **Term.** The terms say a term may be month-to-month or fixed, renews automatically at "then-current pricing", and paid fees are generally non-refundable. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the term.
- **Ad fees.** If you use Ads Manager, the terms describe a usage fee calculated as a percentage of your ChatGPT ad spend, charged separately from the media bill OpenAI sends you. Setup, managed-service and overage fees are also listed as possibilities.

Fees apply on top of your own labor too. Someone has to review the 25 monthly articles and ship the fixes the platform recommends.

sections.heading: What do you get for the money?
sections.body:
You get repeated sampling across 11 AI surfaces, a prompt bank built from a consumer panel, and tools to act on the gaps. Per Evertune's [FAQ](https://www.evertune.ai/resources/faq), the models monitored include ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, Google AI Overviews, Claude, Copilot, Perplexity, Meta AI and DeepSeek. All of the following are Evertune's own claims; we have not verified them.

- **Statistics.** Each prompt is asked 100 times per model, which Evertune says brings the margin of error to about one point overall and two at topic level.
- **Prompts.** They come from EverPanel, described as more than 150 million real user conversations.
- **Content.** Content Studio drafts articles of 250 to 3,000 words in six templates.
- **Site checks.** [Site Audit](https://www.evertune.ai/platform/site-audit) reviews bot permissions, sitemaps, speed and schema. The pricing page lists "AI website optimization" and bot analytics only under Enterprise, so confirm what Pro includes.

sections.heading: What does Evertune's own site look like to AI crawlers?
sections.body:
Evertune's site is open to AI crawlers. In AEOeye's crawler access study (fetched 2026-10-03, 43 AI-visibility vendor sites), evertune.ai blocked no AI bots in robots.txt: only /legal/ and /404 are disallowed. It also serves a valid llms.txt.

Its homepage HTML carries JSON-LD of type EntryPoint, Organization, SearchAction and WebSite, and the pricing page carries none. That means prices are plain text rather than structured Offer markup, though JavaScript may inject schema we did not see. This is a neutral fact box, not a verdict on the product. See [the study](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory) and its [per-site CSV](/resources/ai-crawler-access-study-2026-10.csv).

sections.heading: Who is Evertune worth it for?
sections.body:
Evertune is worth it if you will use both halves: measurement and action. That means a team with a content owner, appetite for ChatGPT ads, and a budget of $9,600 a year or more. Evertune's own pitch is built around that loop.

![Digital payment terminal on a wooden desk next to cash and receipts](https://images.pexels.com/photos/3570241/pexels-photo-3570241.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

It is probably not worth it if you only want to know whether AI engines name you. [Generative engine optimization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_engine_optimization) (GEO) means improving visibility in AI-generated answers, and the [original GEO paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735) reports visibility gains of up to 40% in its benchmark. But you can learn your starting point for far less before you pay for repeated sampling.

AEOeye's free audit asks ChatGPT three unbranded buyer questions and shows the real answers and the competitors named instead. The $29 one-time report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity across 10 questions. It is a snapshot, not a tracker. For ongoing monitoring, compare [Evertune alternatives](/alternatives/evertune), the [side-by-side](/vs/evertune) and [the full tool comparison](/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools), then [run the free audit](/) first.

keyTakeaways: Evertune lists Pro at $800 a month and Enterprise as custom, quote-only; the billing term for Pro is not stated.
No free trial is mentioned anywhere on evertune.ai; every plan routes to a demo request.
The old ~$3,000-a-month figure is unverified and does not appear on Evertune's current pages.
Ask what "100,000 prompts" counts, which fees apply to your order, and the term and renewal rules before you sign.
It pays off if you will use the content and ChatGPT-ads side; to see whether AI names you, check for free first.

faqs.q: Does Evertune have a free trial?
faqs.a: No free trial is mentioned on Evertune's pricing, plan or FAQ pages as of 3 October 2026. The only call to action is "Request a demo", and the Pro sign-up page says a team member will walk you through your first report. It does not say whether that report is free, so ask before booking.

The pricing page lists Pro at $800 / month, with 100,000 prompts tracked across 11 AI models, 25 AI-optimized articles a month, three onboarding sessions, affiliate advertising partnerships and AI Retargeting. It does not say whether billing is monthly or annual, so confirm the term. $800 × 12 = $9,600 a year at list price.

faqs.q: How much does Evertune Enterprise cost?
faqs.a: Evertune does not publish it. The pricing page says "Custom" and routes you to a demo request. Enterprise adds a dedicated AI Success Manager, unlimited content generation, AI website optimization, AI bot analytics and SSO to everything in Pro. Ask for a written quote including setup and renewal terms.

We could not verify that. Some older third-party comparisons report it, but Evertune's current pricing page lists Pro at $800 a month and Enterprise as custom. Treat $3,000 as an outdated or unconfirmed estimate and get any real figure from Evertune directly, in writing.

faqs.q: What is a cheaper way to check whether AI recommends my brand?
faqs.a: AEOeye's free audit asks ChatGPT three buyer questions and shows the full answers and the competitors named. The $29 one-time report covers 10 questions across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity. Neither is a tracker, so for daily monitoring across many prompts you need a dedicated tool.
